description: Repair FF-input insertion boundary and retry the unchanged pair
proposal: Family: parameter tying. Current retained frontier is 1,518 parameters at 99.010000%, a +0.010000-point margin. There have been 73 prior macro-attempts and 626 prior micro-trials in this family. The most recent accepted result is attempt-0173/micro-0002 at 1,518/99.01%; the most recent failed result is attempt-0175/micro-0001, an unscored automation error caused by inserting candidate pair 147/40 into the LayerNorm bias tie list. This is the permitted exact repair: change only the helper boundary to the closing delimiter immediately before FF_OUT_TIED_PAIRS, while retaining pair ranking, exclusion set, incumbent, and candidate conditions. Hypothesis remains that FF-input pair 147/40 can qualify after excluding catastrophic pair 233/91. The helper adds one ordered FF-input union per official micro-trial with runner-only retention/rollback. Stop at first scored discard/error, no pair, 20 trials, or 25 minutes. Repairing the untested candidate is more informative than choosing a new pair because attempt 175 produced no architectural evidence.
summary: After the exact boundary repair, all 20 ordered FF-input unions in the capped band qualified. The retained frontier moved from 1,518 to 1,498 parameters; no scored discards or runner errors occurred in the repaired macro. Compute used 20 official migrations/verifications over about 24m30s. Stop reason: hard micro-trial cap, not a measured failure boundary. This confirms attempt 175 was an automation-only error.
